body.summary: Urgent: risk of an ER visit or hospital admission in the next 7 days is 6% (urgent line 6%, typical day 1.2%). Risk of a rough patch in the next 7 days: 22% (alert line 16%). The treatment calendar alone gives 9%; their check-ins move it +5 points and wearable signals +8. Biggest driver: Sleep efficiency 87% vs usual 92%, waking 3.5x a night vs 2.0x, 6.8 h asleep vs 7.1 h.

profile.context: Day 5 of cycle 4 (IV chemo every 21 days)

evidence.label: Sleep
evidence.text: Sleep efficiency 87% vs usual 92%, waking 3.5x a night vs 2.0x, 6.8 h asleep vs 7.1 h

evidence.label: Steps
evidence.text: Steps 38% below their usual (7,721 vs 12,395 a day, last 3 days)

evidence.label: Check-ins
evidence.text: Skipped the last 3 daily check-ins (people report a rough day 1.4x as often after 3+ skips); 1 coaching call(s) missed or moved in 4 weeks; their last rating was their usual 4/5 (ratings up to 3 days ago)

evidence.label: Treatment calendar
evidence.text: Day 5 of cycle 4 (IV chemo every 21 days). The calendar alone predicts 9% risk of a rough patch this week.

recommendations.action: Call today. Ask how they feel, about fever, fluids and anything new. If anything is off, have them call their care team now.
recommendations.why: Their wearable pattern matches the days before an ER visit or hospital stay. The coach does not diagnose; the care team decides.

recommendations.action: Check in this week about sleep: nights, naps, worries. Share the sleep tips sheet.
recommendations.why: Sleep got shorter or more broken than usual.

recommendations.action: Move the next coaching call earlier and plan around the expected low point.
recommendations.why: The forecast covers the next 7 days.

recommendations.action: Send a short, no-pressure message asking how the week is going; offer a 2-minute call instead of the form.
recommendations.why: 3 daily check-ins skipped in a row; rough days are more common after a run of skips.

demo.note: Hidden from the coach view: what actually happened in the 14 days after the forecast.

definition.rough_day: relative to the person: daily feeling 1, or 2+ points below their own median of the last 28 check-ins (until 5 check-ins: feeling <= 2); OR on the weekly check-in any of fatigue, nausea, pain, appetite loss, diarrhea, trouble sleeping, anxiety, sadness >= 3 or 2+ above their own usual; OR ER visit / admission / treatment paused. Skipped check-ins are not counted as rough; they are shown to the coach as a warning sign (rough rate on return rises ~1.8x after 5 skips) with a same-day wearable estimate
definition.rough_patch: a rough day followed by another within 3 days, or any clinical event; onset = first patch day after 7 quiet days
definition.forecast: each evening, P(rough patch onset in the next 7 days); days already inside a patch are not scored
definition.early_warning: an alert counts only if it fires 2+ days before onset
definition.inputs: the person's own check-ins vs their usual (feeling, weekly symptoms; values up to 3 days ago), skipped check-ins and missed coaching calls, wearable signals vs personal baseline, wear time, known treatment schedule. No events, no diary text.
definition.split: by patient: 60% train, 15% validation (thresholds), 25% test (all numbers below)
definition.alert_budget: thresholds put 5% of quiet validation days on alert, same budget for every method

urgent.definition: P(ER visit or hospital admission in the next 7 days); urgent when in the top 3% of validation days. Separate flag; does not change the rough-patch status.
